fit: extra-virgin olive oil comparator with oxybutynin in overactive bladder
assessment: The registered outcome was daily void count. Both groups received oxybutynin and the trial stopped with 31 participants and no posted results. There is no separately estimated oil effect or Parkinson cohort.

fit: conflicting placebo identity in the saw palmetto urinary trial
assessment: The paper describes olive oil as comparator in a study of IPSS and OABSS totals. The exact linked registration instead specifies polyethylene glycol-400. Actual oil exposure remains unresolved and no separate urgency or frequency result is given.

fit: multi-food dietary pattern and general urinary complaints in Parkinsonism
assessment: In 1205 participants the MIND score was inversely associated with general urinary symptom severity. The Mediterranean score was inconclusive. The outcome is broader than urgency frequency, and neither score isolates extra-virgin olive oil.

fit: black tea brew and horizontal rat open-field crossings
assessment: Tea-only and water groups showed an inconclusive crossing difference at 12 weeks. The test assesses spontaneous activity and is not a Parkinson bradykinesia measure. Twenty allocated versus ten in the outcome table.

fit: black tea brew and acute rat hole-board exploration
assessment: Tea increased exploratory crossings after acute administration. Means were nonmonotonic across doses. Healthy rats and an exploration count do not provide a bradykinesia estimate.

fit: solid dark chocolate and measured postbiopsy anxiety
assessment: Randomized non-Parkinson trial reported postbiopsy anxiety scores 34.31 versus 38.89 with a group-by-time p = .01. No matched snack and masking limitations leave expectancy unresolved.

fit: dark chocolate and HADS anxiety in severe chronic fatigue
assessment: In a ten-person masked crossover, median HADS anxiety fell during high-cocoa treatment and rose during the simulated chocolate period. Period baselines differed. Within-treatment tests do not supply a separate paired treatment contrast.

fit: brewed cocoa with caffeine and anxiety during a task
assessment: The published anxiety interaction favored caffeinated cocoa against caffeine alone. Cocoa versus placebo did not have a detectable mood interaction. The drink and mental challenge differ from ordinary dark chocolate and Parkinson anxiety.

fit: dark chocolate and biomarkers in a rotenone Parkinson model
assessment: The original report includes a chocolate group and several biochemical, microbiota and histology outcomes. It has no scored anxiety behavior or clinical anxiety measure.
